title: Runway Optimizer: experiment lifecycle, gating, and ownership
creator: Aisha N. Patel
description: Objective: Establish a repeatable experiment lifecycle, gating rules, and clear ownership for Runway Optimizer experiments that aim to improve per-token economics via adaptive batching, prefix/KV caching TTLs, and selective quantization. Scope: covers field trials, canary rollouts on Dedicated pools, metric gating, and rollback protocol. Success metric: 15-25% average token-cost reduction on candidate workloads without >3% quality regression on tracked prompt sets. Deliverables: experiment template (hypothesis -> design -> safety gates), standardized dashboard slices for econ and quality, automation for canary traffic shaping, owner/runbook template, and a preflight checklist for security/compliance and SRE readiness.
acceptance_criteria: Template present in Confluence with sections: hypothesis, datasets, metric definitions, rollout plan, rollback triggers
Automationized canary that routes <=5% traffic to new config with timed rollback if econ/quality gates fail
Dashboards for token-cost, p50/p95 latency, error rate, and quality-regression tied to canonical prompt set
Owner assigned for each experiment phase (design, run, analyze, rollout)
Documented sign-off matrix including PM, Eng, Research, SRE, and Security
updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created. Kickoff scheduled with Serving Runtime, Research, and SRE. Initial scope drafted.
2025-02-18: Research provided candidate quant profiles (4-bit and mixed 8/4) for two model families. Linked doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Runway-Optimizer-Quant-Profiles
2025-02-25: Eng runs baseline cost/loss measurement on sample workload A. Baseline dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/fieldlab/runway-baseline?orgId=1
2025-02-28: Design review feedback: prefer staged TTL increases for KV caching rather than global long-lived TTLs to reduce over-caching. Action: add TTL sweep strategy to template.
2025-03-03: SRE review: requested explicit circuit-breaker thresholds and an automated emergency rollback PR (see GH PR #3217). GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3217

2025-03-05: Canary automation prototype merged to infra branch (PR #3229). Began internal smoke run at 1% traffic for 4 hours. Observed 18% cost reduction on hashed requests; quality delta +0.8% on held prompt set.
risks: Quality regression risk when combining aggressive quantization with prefix cache eviction — mitigated by gated canaries and per-prompt monitoring
Operational risk if autoscale interactions cause head-of-line blocking at higher batch sizes — mitigation: SRE load tests before rollout
Billing attribution complexity for mixed-mode routing during canary — mitigation: tagging and separate cost buckets on dashboards
notes: Owner model: PM owns success criteria; Eng (serving-runtime) owns rollout automation; Research owns quant profiles and evaluation harness; SRE owns canary infra and circuit breakers.
Experiment lifecycle: 1) Hypothesis & dataset selection, 2) Local validation & offline sims, 3) Canary (timeboxed), 4) Analysis & sign-off, 5) Progressive rollout, 6) Post-rollout audit.
Suggested metric gates: token-cost delta <= -12%, p95 latency change <= +10%, quality regression <= +1.5% absolute on canonical prompts, error rate < 0.2%
next_steps: Finalize preflight checklist and circulate for sign-off by 2025-03-10
Expand canary to 5% traffic on non-critical customers for 24 hours once SRE load test passes
Run a controlled AB evaluation for combined batching+kv-ttl+quant config to validate interactions
Prepare rollout communications and customer-facing FAQ for potential behavior changes
